# Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga Pācittiya 37 (Bu-Vb Pc37)

**ID:** Bu-Vb Pc37  
**Section:** Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga (bu-vb)  
**Collection:** Vinaya  
**Title (Pali):** Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga Pācittiya 37  
**Title (English, from literature):** Eating at the wrong time  
**tipitaka.org (CST):** [https://tipitaka.org/romn/cscd/vin02m1.mul0.xml](https://tipitaka.org/romn/cscd/vin02m1.mul0.xml)

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga Pācittiya 37, titled *Vikālabhojana* ("Eating at the wrong time"), establishes that a monk who consumes solid or soft food between noon and dawn commits an offense requiring confession (*pācittiya*). According to the Vibhaṅga, the prohibition was laid down at Rājagaha to forbid eating during the improper period (*vikāla*) [Entrance to the Vinaya 1983]. Under standard monastic discipline, the allowable period for taking meals was restricted to the hours from sunrise until midday [Wijayaratna 1990].

This training rule is central to accounts of the Second Buddhist Council [Bapat 1956; Hazra 2002; Sarao & Long 2017]. The Vajjian monks claimed as allowable the *dvaṅgulakappa*—the practice of consuming food past midday when the shadow was within two finger-breadths or digits wide—which the council ruled unlawful because it directly contravened Pācittiya 37 [Bapat 1956; Hazra 2002; Sarao & Long 2017; Entrance to the Vinaya 1983].
